messages:
Incident Bot: [INC-2026-042] 03:42 UTC - High latency on /v1/generate (region: us-east-1). Paging oncall: Alex. Severity: P1.

Maya (CS): Alex — saw the page, thanks for picking up. Acme Corp reported degraded experience. Can you summarize customer-visible impact so we can prepare a follow-up?

Alex (oncall): Root handoff note: brief spike in tail latency starting 03:41. Autoscaler failed to spin new dedicated workers due to a regression in the capacity filter. Fallback routing to smaller model pool started at 03:50 which brought error rate down but increased latency for long prompts.

Sam (eng-sre): Oncall now. quick summary: 03:41 spike due to KV cache eviction when high-concurrency prefix churned; autoscaler filter prevented new pool from being used (bug in label matching after deploy). Mitigation timeline below.

Maya (CS): Ok — team needs: 1) short status page update, 2) customer-facing email draft for Acme, 3) proposed credit and next steps. I can send AC if we agree.

Alex (oncall): Timeline (working):
- 03:41 UTC: error/latency spike observed by metrics + Acme report
- 03:43: pager triggered to oncall
- 03:46: initial mitigation attempt (scale-up) failed due to label-filter bug
- 03:50: fallback routing -> smaller model pool (manual route) started, errors dropped by 95%
- 04:10: autoscaler fix deployed, normal routing resumed by 04:18
- 04:25: monitoring stable, incident declared resolved

Sam (eng-sre): Preliminary root cause: two concurrent issues: 1) cache eviction under extreme prefix churn reduced effective throughput; 2) deploy introduced a label-matching regression in autoscaler that blocked capacity provisioning for affected pools. Both necessary for P1.

Priya (PM): Noted customer impact: Acme had ~40% of their requests hitting increased latency window (03:41-04:18), and some requests retried. We need clear mitigation and commitments.

Maya (CS): Draft status page update (suggested):

```
Status: Partial degradation (Resolved)
Impact: Some customers experienced increased latency and request errors for the text generation API in us-east-1.
Start: 2026-04-12 03:41 UTC
End: 2026-04-12 04:25 UTC
Details: A combination of cache eviction under high prefix churn and an autoscaler label-matching regression prevented new capacity from being provisioned, which increased latency until manual fallback routing and a code fix restored normal operation.
What we did: Rolled out an autoscaler fix, routed traffic to compatible model pools, and monitored system recovery.
Next steps: Full RCA will be published within 3 business days. Customers impacted directly will be contacted with timeline clarifications and compensation options.
```

Maya (CS): Draft customer email to Acme (short/simple):

```
Hi Team —

Sorry for the disruption earlier today. Between 03:41 and 04:25 UTC we experienced increased latency and some errors on the text generation API in us-east-1 which affected requests from your account. We mitigated the issue by routing traffic to compatible pools and deploying a fix to our autoscaler.

We understand this impacted your users and are preparing a short RCA and a restitution proposal. Proposed immediate action: a one-time billing credit equivalent to 24 hours of your average usage at the affected endpoints, plus a follow-up sync if you'd like.

I can send the full RCA and credit details by EOD tomorrow. Would you prefer an in-product notice or an email?

Thanks and very sorry —
Maya, Customer Success (Redwood)
```

Jordan (support): That looks good. Suggest removing the phrase "some errors" — be specific: "increased error rate and higher tail latency". Also include link to status page when we post.

Maya (CS): Good call. I'll update.

Sam (eng-sre): For RCA bullets to include to customer:
- What happened (concise)
- Why it happened (cache eviction + autoscaler label regression)
- How we fixed it (manual routing + code fix)
- How we'll prevent recurrence (patch + improved canary + autoscaler test coverage + KV cache threshold tuning)

Alex (oncall): Preventative actions (short):
- Revert/patch label matching logic + add unit/integration tests
- Add tighter canary for autoscaler changes (synthetic load test at low traffic)
- Increase KV cache protection for hot prefixes and add metrics alert on churn
- Run playbook walkthrough with oncall team weekly for next 2 months

Priya (PM): Proposed customer credit rationale: 24h-equivalent credit (easy to calculate and meaningful). For enterprise customers like Acme, also offer an optional technical sync + prioritized assistance on their traffic patterns.

Maya (CS): Proposed credit language: "We are offering a one-time billing credit equivalent to 24 hours of typical usage on the affected endpoints, plus a technical sync if desired."

Jordan (support): Approve. Also cc Sales/AM when we send credit details.

Alex (oncall): One more: please don't promise timeline for full RCA beyond '3 business days' unless Eng agrees — they may want 48h.

Sam (eng-sre): We can target 48 hours for a preliminary RCA and 3 business days for the full writeup.

Maya (CS): Okay final checklist for send:
- [ ] Update status page (I will post)
- [ ] Send edited email to Acme and cc Sales/AM
- [ ] Include preliminary RCA in customer email (48h) and full RCA in 3 business days
- [ ] Propose credit 24h-equivalent and note how it will be applied

Priya (PM): Sounds good. Priya -> will coordinate prioritization and track the RCA timeline with Sam.

Jordan (support): I'll prepare internal note for AM + include suggested Slack snippet for Sales to share with Acme if they reach out.

Maya (CS): Thanks everyone. I'll post the status page update now and draft the email. If there are any wording objections ping me within 15m, otherwise I'll send. :thumbsup:

Alex (oncall): Thanks team. Oncall will follow up with details for the RCA.

Sam (eng-sre): Leaving logs and traces in the incident channel now for postmortem.

Maya (CS): Sending now. Will attach logs link and credit calc to the email thread once Sam posts.

Jordan (support): Confirmed. I'll be on the outgoing thread for AM visibility.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-2026-042 marked resolved at 04:25 UTC.

Maya (CS): Thread closed for initial customer outreach — reopening for any further clarifications after RCA.

Priya (PM): Great. Follow-up sync scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 UTC to review preliminary RCA.
